title: Customer portal login: password hashing that is less random than it looks
name: Portal password hashing

questions.prompt: A security review of a database snapshot found that every customer who signed up with the same password has an identical stored hash, and in fact every hash in the table starts with the same 32 characters. Logins work normally. Fix portal/passwords.py so the tests pass.

tests.content:
import unittest

from portal.passwords import hash_password, verify_password
from portal.service import AuthError, AuthService
from portal.store import AccountStore


class Clock:
    def __init__(self):
        self.now = 1000.0

    def __call__(self):
        return self.now


def make():
    clock = Clock()
    store = AccountStore()
    return AuthService(store, clock), store, clock


class AuthTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_registered_user_can_log_in(self):
        svc, store, _ = make()
        svc.register("ana@example.com", "correct horse")
        self.assertEqual(svc.login("ANA@example.com", "correct horse").email, "ana@example.com")
        session = svc.login_session("ana@example.com", "correct horse")
        self.assertEqual(svc.sessions.lookup(session.token).email, "ana@example.com")

    def test_wrong_password_is_rejected(self):
        svc, store, _ = make()
        svc.register("ana@example.com", "correct horse")
        with self.assertRaises(AuthError):
            svc.login("ana@example.com", "battery staple")

    def test_stored_hash_does_not_contain_the_password(self):
        svc, store, _ = make()
        svc.register("ana@example.com", "correct horse")
        self.assertNotIn("correct horse", store.get("ana@example.com").password_hash)

    def test_explicit_salt_gives_a_reproducible_hash(self):
        salt = bytes(range(16))
        self.assertEqual(hash_password("pw-12345678", salt), hash_password("pw-12345678", salt))
        self.assertTrue(verify_password("pw-12345678", hash_password("pw-12345678", salt)))

    def test_two_users_with_the_same_password_get_different_salts(self):
        svc, store, _ = make()
        svc.register("ana@example.com", "hunter2hunter2")
        svc.register("bob@example.com", "hunter2hunter2")
        a = store.get("ana@example.com").password_hash
        b = store.get("bob@example.com").password_hash
        print("ana:", a[:24] + "...")
        print("bob:", b[:24] + "...")
        self.assertNotEqual(a.split("$")[0], b.split("$")[0], "both accounts were given the same salt")
        self.assertNotEqual(a, b, "identical passwords produced identical stored hashes")

    def test_hashing_the_same_password_twice_gives_different_records(self):
        self.assertNotEqual(hash_password("same-password"), hash_password("same-password"))

    def test_account_locks_after_three_failures(self):
        svc, store, clock = make()
        svc.register("ana@example.com", "correct horse")
        for _ in range(3):
            with self.assertRaises(AuthError):
                svc.login("ana@example.com", "nope")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AuthError, "locked"):
            svc.login("ana@example.com", "correct horse")
        clock.now += 301
        self.assertEqual(svc.login("ana@example.com", "correct horse").email, "ana@example.com")

    def test_unknown_email_gets_the_same_error_as_a_bad_password(self):
        svc, store, _ = make()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AuthError, "invalid credentials"):
            svc.login("ghost@example.com", "whatever1")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
